title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-35
content:
Notes to self - GPU ops (quick)

Date: 2026-03-04
Context: personal scratchpad while triaging capacity spike for dedicated pools + followups from yesterday's maintenance window.

Top priorities:
- Finalize hotfix for GPU allocator leak (PR 456) — patch landed on staging, need to push to canary. Confirm memory regressions gone.
  - run: ./tools/gpu-health.sh --nodes tainted-canary (today 10:30 PT)
  - check logs: /var/log/gpu-allocator/*.log for OOM traces
- Autoscale config for dedicated-gpupool-3 still overshooting under short bursts
  - hypothesis: burst cooldown too short (current 60s), bump to 180s for canary
  - metric to watch: pods/second scale events, token throughput per GPU
- Network: intermittent NVLink error on node gnode-17 (seen 03/03 22:12)
  - repro steps: run bin/nvlink-test -t 120 on gnode-17
  - if fails, reseat NVLink cable + reboot (notify SRE before reboot)
  - open ticket INF-2345 assigned to Ravi for hardware escalation if persists

Quick TODO list:
- [ ] Push allocator hotfix to canary cluster (Avery) — target 2026-03-04 11:00 PT
- [ ] Update autoscaler cooldown and create metric alert (Elena)
- [ ] Run gpu-health.sh across all dedicated-pools (batch, then rolling)
- [ ] Post short postmortem note in #gpu-ops about yesterday's spike (include CPU+IO graphs)
- [ ] Confirm JIT kernel regression test in CI (link to PR 456)

Observations from yesterday:
- Spike correlated with large batch ingestion from customer X during 21:30-22:00 UTC — probably prefix caching miss + sudden model switch (v1-prod -> v2-quant)
- Some nodes reported high nvlink retries but cleared after restarting launcher on that node

Commands/snippets to run:
- Check GPU mem usage across cluster:
  kubectl -n infra get pods -o wide | grep gpupool-3
  kubectl top nodes --no-headers | sort -k3 -n
- Run health script against list (example):
  for N in $(cat canary-nodes.txt); do ssh $N 'sudo /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-health.sh --full' || echo $N >> failed-nodes.txt; done
- Reproduce NVLink test:
  ssh gnode-17 'sudo /opt/redwood/bin/nvlink-test -t 120 -r 5'

Questions / followups:
- Does autoscaler respect container startupProbe delay? If probe is slow during heavy load, we might scale prematurely. Ask Elena to confirm.
- Need clearer SLAs for dedicated burst capacity — update runbook with thresholds and contact for sales/CS for any customer-facing limits.

Notes to include in followup doc:
- Timeline of events (UTC): 21:28 spike start, 21:41 peak, 21:58 tapering, 22:12 nvlink retry log on gnode-17, 22:40 manual launcher restart on gnode-17, 23:05 allocator leak observed on canary logs
- Attach graphs: dedicated-gpupool-3/cpu, mem, nvlink-retries, scale-events (from grafana)

Personal reminders:
- Pair with Ravi 2026-03-05 to review NVLink node health checklist
- Clean up temp debugging containers on canary after patch validated

Rough idea for postmortem outline (short):
- Summary (what happened)
- Impact (customers affected, latency/cost impact)
- Root cause (allocator leak + autoscale cooldown + NVLink flakiness)
- Mitigations (hotfix, autoscale tuning, hardware check)
- Followups (owner + ETA)

End notes: keep this doc terse; expand timeline + attach grafana links before posting.

-- Avery
